author: Cheryl Bush
text: Most people don't really have the luxury of researching which is the most accurate. A person's medical insurance usually determines what is covered and thus affordable for them. The next consideration is usually what fits best into your lifestyle. Libre involves fewer steps to use as compared to dexcom. I don't know about the other brands, but those are the top two. Accuracy is a little bit overrated. Of course you don't want something that's going to be totally inaccurate, but most of the meters are close to the same range of accuracy the people that they work for. Certain meters just don't work well for certain people. The more important thing is using a meter consistently, tracking the results over time, and making adjustments as needed to meet your personal goals. The numbers on the meter are always going to fluctuate. Studies show that meters can measure differently in the same person in the right arm versus the left arm. It's not a matter of which arm is more accurate at a given time. It's a matter of the law of averages over and extended amount of time. I hope this makes sense.
